subject: Hosted API renewal + commit increase — proposal and next steps
messages:
From: Anika Shah <anika@brightlinelabs.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 1 Nov 2028 14:32:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API renewal + commit increase proposal

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the performance improvements were promising for our real-time personalization use case. We're starting our renewal conversation internally and looking at stepping up our monthly committed tokens. Current run-rate hit higher than forecast in Q3 and we'd like to lock in a plan that gives us predictable throughput through next year.

High level ask:
- Move from our current 3M token/month commit to 6M token/month (starting 2029-01-01)
- Keep a soft-burst window for seasonal peaks (Black Friday-like events)
- Clarify per-token rate and any step discounts if we commit annually vs monthly

I can loop procurement once we have a ballpark SOW and pricing. Can you send a proposal and note any ops/latency guarantees tied to the upgrade?

Thanks,
Anika Shah
Head of Product — Brightline Labs
Anika Shah

Attachment: Brightline_Traffic_Oct2028.csv (summary of token trends)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Anika Shah <anika@brightlinelabs.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 2 Nov 2028 09:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API renewal + commit increase proposal

Hi Anika — great to hear Q3 ramped as expected (good problem to have). I pulled together an initial package so we can move procurement and ops in parallel. High level proposal below: 

Offer (summary):
- New monthly committed tokens: 6,000,000/month, 12-month term starting 2029-01-01
- Unit pricing: $0.00035/token on committed tier (first 6M), overage at $0.00050/token with a 10% discounted overage credit for sustained bursts
- Soft-burst: 20% monthly burst buffer included into the first 48 hours of a declared event; longer burst handled via reserved burst credits
- Latency SLA: 95th percentile token latency target consistent with your current profile; we will include a canary fallback policy to maintain availability if one model pool is constrained

Next steps I propose:
1) Ops (karthik) validates configuration and confirms whether the 20% soft-burst needs any dedicated pool changes.
2) I send a draft SOW for review and route to procurement.
3) If procurement agrees, we start a 30-day activation plan to have routing, caching, and billing aligned by Jan 1.

I attached a short SOW template and your traffic CSV for reference. Vanessa, can you confirm whether we have any credit/incentive we can offer for 12-month committed conversion?

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Anika Shah <anika@brightlinelabs.com>

Date: Mon, 6 Nov 2028 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API renewal + commit increase proposal

Thanks Lauren — this looks close to what we need. A few clarifying questions before procurement engages formally: 

1) Can you confirm whether the 20% soft-burst is per month or applied inside a rolling 30-day window? We need to model monthly budgets.
2) For overage credits — how is "sustained bursts" defined (continuous days/hours)?
3) Do you support token-level metering export to our billing system (we'd like a daily export to reconcile usage)?

Procurement: please confirm the vendor onboarding timeline once we have SOW + pricing.

If you're able to provide answers by mid-week, I can get procurement to prioritize the DocuSign review.

-Anika

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 8 Nov 2028 13:55:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Hosted API renewal + commit increase proposal (ops check)

Lauren / Vanessa — quick ops check on the proposed package:
- 6M commit on our hosted pool is straightforward; no infra lock required. We recommend a separate reserved pool for Brightline for predictable QoS during declared events. That gives us isolation for KV cache priming and reduces cold-start tail latency.
- Soft-burst semantics: we implement the 20% soft-burst as a calendar-month buffer by default (cleans at month boundary). If Brightline needs a rolling 30-day model we can do rolling windows but that requires a short billing change and a different aggregation export.
- "Sustained bursts" definition: we use a 24-hour sustained exceed threshold for the discounted overage credit (i.e., if usage > committed + 20% for >24 continuous hours, system tags that period as a sustained event and we apply the agreed overage credit retroactively for that window).
- Metering exports: we can provide a daily CSV export to a secure S3 URL or push to an SFTP endpoint; includes token counts by model and route.

I'll be available to review the SOW and the activation checklist once Lauren shares.

-Karthik
Head of Operations, Redwood Inference
